messages.content: Who is credited with one of the first written plans for an underwater navigation vehicle?
The English mathematician William Bourne recorded one of the first known plans for an underwater navigation vehicle in his 1578 book Inventions or Devises.
What did the Scottish mathematician John Napier write about underwater vessels?
In his 1596 work Secret Inventions, John Napier described devices of sailing under water, among other inventions and strategems, intended for harming enemies.
What kind of work has Harland & Wolff shifted toward in recent years instead of new shipbuilding?
Harland & Wolff has moved toward overhaul, re-fitting, and ship repair work, as well as construction and repair of offshore equipment such as oil platforms, rather than new shipbuilding projects.
What historic vessel did Harland & Wolff win a contract to refurbish in 2011?
Harland & Wolff won the contract to refurbish the SS Nomadic, with structural steel work beginning on 10 February 2011, reconnecting with its nearly 150-year association with the White Star Line.

doc_id: wikipedia:Ship and Offshore Structural Mechanics Laboratory

messages.content: What structural materials were compared in the double-skinned ship collision and grounding experiments?

Six double-skinned structural models were tested under quasi-static loading: four mild steel models and two aluminum alloy models. The mild steel models represented side or bottom structures typical of double hull tankers or LNG carriers, while the aluminum alloy models examined collision and grounding mechanics for aluminum alloy hull vessels.

doc_id: wikipedia:Ship and Offshore Structural Mechanics Laboratory

messages.content: Why were double-skinned structural models used to study ship collision and grounding?

Double-skinned structural models were tested to investigate structural crashworthiness in ship collision and grounding scenarios, varying plate thickness and the initial colliding location to represent realistic double-hull tanker and LNG carrier structures.
What combat system equips the Arleigh Burke-class destroyers built by Ingalls Shipbuilding?
The Arleigh Burke-class destroyers Ingalls Shipbuilding builds are equipped with the US Navy's Aegis Combat System.
How does a yaw angle affect wall-pressure fluctuations on a hull during a turning maneuver?

Introducing a yaw angle systematically increases wall-pressure fluctuation levels across the entire frequency spectrum. The effect is monotonic with yaw angle: higher yaw angles produce uniformly higher power spectral density levels than lower yaw angles, which are in turn higher than the straight-ahead baseline condition.
What were the main gun changes made to the Royal Sovereign-class battleships compared to their original design?

The Royal Sovereign class was originally intended to carry a new wire-wound, 40-caliber 12-inch gun, but was instead fitted with 13.5-inch guns similar to those on the Admirals-series ships, since the design required four of the heaviest guns available.
What happened to the New Mexico-class battleships after World War II?

New Mexico and Idaho returned to the US east coast by October 1945 and were decommissioned, then stricken from the naval register in 1947 and sold for scrap. Mississippi instead survived the postwar drawdown by being converted into a gunnery training and evaluation ship, reconstructed at the Norfolk Naval Shipyard from November 1945 through April 1948.
How did the wider beam of the Florida-class battleships affect their stability?

The Florida-class ships had a beam of 88 feet 3 inches, wider than the preceding Delaware class, and this wider beam increased the vessels' metacentric height, which is a key measure of a ship's initial stability.
What were the principal dimensions of the Florida-class battleships?

The Florida-class ships were 510 feet long at the waterline and 521 feet 6 inches overall, with a beam of 88 feet 3 inches and a draft of 28 feet 6 inches, displacing 21,825 long tons at standard displacement.
What survivability advantage do dry-tank wave energy converters have, and what challenge remains?

Dry-tank wave energy converters (En-WECs) naturally have improved survivability compared to conventional wet-tank designs (Ex-WECs). However, a remaining challenge is that the internal mechanical oscillator can only be tuned to one frequency, and as the system's stiffness, friction, or lubrication varies over time, the oscillator's natural frequency drifts away from its pre-tuned value, reducing energy transfer efficiency.
Which companies received early contracts to build PT boats in 1939?

On 25 May 1939, Higgins Industries received a contract for two boats of the Sparkman & Stephens design, scaled to 81 feet overall. On 8 June 1939, Miami Shipbuilding and Fisher Boatworks each received contracts for two boats of the Crouch design, and the Philadelphia Navy Yard was contracted for two 81-foot boats of its own design.
What caused the high bulk carrier loss rates in the early 1990s?

In 1990, 20 bulk carriers sank, killing 94 crew, and in 1991, 24 sank, killing 154. The American Bureau of Shipping concluded the losses were directly traceable to failure of the cargo hold structure, while Lloyd's Register added that hull sides could not withstand the combination of local corrosion, fatigue cracking, and operational damage.
What was OpenFLASH validated against in the described study?

OpenFLASH's results were validated against Capytaine, with the study also clarifying block matrix structure and asymptotic behaviour at small and large frequencies, and discussing numerical subtleties needed to avoid overflow and finite precision effects.
What is water entry hydrodynamics concerned with, based on the naval hydrodynamics literature?

Water entry hydrodynamics studies the impact of two-dimensional sections entering water, including cases with and without flow separation, such as flow separation occurring from chines, as investigated at symposia on naval and numerical ship hydrodynamics.
What structural element is studied for vortex-induced vibration in the paper on flexible viscoelastic fluid-conveying risers?

The paper studies the three-dimensional vortex-induced vibration nonlinear dynamics of a flexible viscoelastic fluid-conveying riser, a structure relevant to offshore riser systems that carry fluid and are subject to vortex shedding from surrounding currents.
How does the vortex shedding mode affect the streamwise vorticity concentration downstream of a cylinder?

The vortex shedding mode inhibits fluid shearing along the interface of vortex wakes, causing the streamwise secondary structure to vanish and the streamwise vorticity concentration to weaken downstream, which produces a recovery of the two-dimensional hydrodynamic response along the cylinder.
How is the scattering of flexural gravity waves by a submerged porous disc under ice cover typically analyzed?

Under linear theory, the problem is reduced to a hypersingular boundary integral equation, which can be further reduced to a system of one-dimensional Fredholm integral equations of the second kind, allowing the hydrodynamic force, added mass, and damping coefficients to be computed numerically.
How well did the SWASH model compare against a boundary element method (BEM) for a ship-shaped vessel's wave diffraction and radiation problems?

SWASH captured the typical magnitude and phase of the excitation forces and moment for the diffraction problem across the tested wave periods. For the radiation problem, discrepancies between SWASH and BEM were typically larger, but SWASH still captured the variation and typical magnitude of the added mass and radiation damping for all degrees of freedom.
How were the coefficients of Morison's equation established to mimic an existing white-box model in the machine learning study?

The coefficients of Morison's equation were established via Bayesian Linear Regression using the complete validation set, which would not ordinarily be used in white-box model creation, then kept constant while the amount of training data coverage was varied.
How does the boundary layer concept from naval architecture explain resistance on a ship hull?

As a ship moves through water, which is not an ideal fluid, fluid particles cling to the hull due to adhesive force between water and the ship. This creates a boundary layer with a steep speed gradient: the fluid in contact with the hull has approximately zero relative velocity, while fluid at the edge of the boundary layer moves at the free-stream speed, and this velocity gradient is a source of resistance.
What role do spectral wave models like SWAN play in coastal wave modeling, and what is their limitation?

Spectral wave models such as SWAN translate large-scale metocean conditions into coastal wave characteristics and efficiently simulate wind-wave generation, energy dissipation, shoaling, and nonlinear wave-wave interactions. However, their underlying assumptions limit their ability to capture strongly nonlinear wave transformations and pronounced diffraction effects, which is why phase-resolving models become necessary for accurately simulating complex coastal conditions.
Why does mooring dynamics modeling approach matter for a moored floating box subjected to significant motions?

It has been demonstrated that for floating structures subjected to significant motions, a dynamic mooring model produces notably different mooring tensions compared to a quasi-static mooring model, which is why FloatStepper integrates its wave solver with state-of-the-art mooring line algorithms such as those used by MDD, OrcaFlex, Moody, and MoorDyn.
What is a twisted-toroid propeller, and what advantage does it offer over traditional propellers?

A twisted-toroid, or ring-shaped, propeller replaces conventional blades with a circular ring. It is significantly quieter, particularly at audible frequencies, and more efficient than traditional propellers for both air and water applications, because the design distributes the vortices generated by the propeller across the entire shape, causing them to dissipate faster.
How is thruster fault tolerance handled in the control law for an eight-thruster underwater vehicle?

The control law and unlocking strategy are derived using discrete Linear Quadratic Tracking (LQT) combined with Bayesian posterior probability weighting, and the algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations including scenarios with two thruster failures, comparing soft and hard switching in a horizontal thruster configuration.
What are the main environmental excitation forces that a dynamic positioning system must counteract?

A dynamic positioning system must counteract environmental excitation forces that push the ship from its target position and heading: wind forces, wave forces, and current forces. Because of the ship's mass, it is not responsive to fast variations in these exciting forces, and the flow phenomena of waves and current in the water also affect thruster performance.
What power source is being explored as a potentially unlimited option for ship propulsion?

Nuclear fusion is being explored as a potentially unlimited power source for ships, a topic examined by researchers from the Department of Maritime and Transport Technology at Delft University of Technology together with the Belgian Nuclear Research Centre.
How does the fuel injection system in the Detroit Diesel V8 engine meter and deliver fuel?

A mechanical or electric fuel lift pump feeds a Stanadyne rotary distributor injection pump at low pressure. This pump controls both metering, via an internal centrifugal governor, and high pressure fuel delivery to the injectors, which atomize fuel at high pressure into a hemispherical Inconel prechamber using Bosch pintle and seat mechanical injectors, an indirect injection design.
How do propellers use fins to generate thrust for a ship?

Propellers use a number of rotating fins, also called foils or blades, to translate torquing force into lateral thrust. Foil-shaped fins generate thrust when moved because the lift they produce sets the surrounding water in motion and pushes the fin, and the vessel, in the opposite direction.
How does the MPC-based reinforcement learning method handle an autonomous surface vessel's freight mission with disturbances?

A parametrized MPC scheme approximates the optimal policy, considering tracking and docking costs along with state constraints (position, velocity) and input constraints (thruster force, angle). A Least Squares Temporal Difference-based deterministic policy gradient method then tunes the parameters inside the MPC model, cost, and constraints so the vessel achieves a close-to-optimal policy for collision-free path tracking, docking, and the transition between them.
Why might an underwater vehicle's thruster fault detection scheme avoid needing an additional state observer?

Most practical underwater vehicles already combine an acoustic positioning system, a Doppler velocity log (DVL), and an inertial measurement unit (IMU) for navigation, so from a control engineering standpoint there is no need for an additional observer to estimate the vehicle's states; tracking or regulation errors from the existing redundant systems can instead be used directly to construct a residual for detecting thruster faults.
What are the main building blocks of an FPSO?

An FPSO is built from an accommodation block for life support, a hull for support and marine systems storage, topsides for separation and impurity removal, a shuttle tanker for export to market, a mooring system for station keeping, and risers to import and export fluids.
Why are FPSOs a popular choice for offshore oil and gas development?

FPSOs are suitable for a wide range of water depths and environmental conditions, do not require extensive infield infrastructure, can be used for both oil and gas developments, and can be tailored to suit specific field characteristics.
What mooring configurations can embedded anchor piles support for offshore structures?

Embedded anchor piles, which are driven or drilled and provide large holding capacity, support three types of mooring configurations: vertical tethers, catenary moorings, and semi-taut or taut moorings, used for structures such as offshore wind turbines, FPSOs, and floating LNG facilities.
When are steel gravity base structures (GBS) typically used for offshore platforms?

Steel GBS are predominantly used where there is no or limited availability of crane barges to install a conventional fixed offshore platform, such as in the Caspian Sea. They are usually anchored directly onto the seabed and typically do not provide hydrocarbon storage capability, being installed by wet-tow or dry-tow and self-installed via controlled ballasting.
What is the TetraSpar floating wind platform concept and how is it assembled?

TetraSpar is a tension-leg platform design with replaceable pressurized tanks anchored to sheet walls, assembled from smaller modules. The prototype, built in Grenaa and commissioned in Norway in December 2021, uses a 3.6 MW Siemens turbine at a 65 meter draught in 200 meter water depth, and by 2024 achieved an overall capacity factor of 54% with 97 to 99% availability.
How is gas pressure increased along the route of UK-Ireland Interconnector No. 1?

Gas is first raised to 85 bar pressure at a compressor station near the Beattock Compressor Station, then transported via a 36-inch buried overland pipeline to Brighouse Bay, where the Brighouse compressor station raises the pressure further to 140 bar before it continues through a subsea pipeline.
What design guidance does API RP 2FPS provide for floating production systems?

API RP 2FPS gives a high-level specification for the design and analysis of floating production systems such as semi-submersibles, spars, FPSOs, and conversion/reuse of existing structures, defining design environmental criteria, accident loads, and fire and blast loads.
Why is vortex-induced vibration (VIV) particularly important to study in circular cylindrical offshore structures?

VIV occurs when fluid flowing past a quasi-cylindrical structure generates oscillations due to vortex shedding on either side, creating forces perpendicular to the flow. This is crucial to study because these oscillations can cause structural damage or failure, especially in structures like marine risers and floating platforms that are subjected to fluctuating fluid loads.
What offshore disaster involving a semi-submersible drill rig occurred in 1982?
The Ocean Ranger, a semi-submersible drill rig, collapsed in a storm off the east coast of Canada in 1982, with the loss of all 84 crew members.
What is the difference between semi-submersible and pontoon-type very large floating structures?

Semi-submersible VLFS designs have a raised platform above sea level supported by column tubes, making them more suitable for deployment in high seas with large waves since they minimize wave effects while maintaining constant buoyant force; they are commonly used for petroleum exploration in deep waters and are fixed in place by column tubes, piles, or bracing systems. Pontoon-type VLFS platforms instead rest on the water surface.
What structures make up the Kizomba A deepwater oil project, and what was notable about its FPSO?

The Kizomba A project consists of a tension leg platform (TLP) and an FPSO, which receives oil from the wells for storage until transfer to tankers. At the time of its construction, the Kizomba A FPSO was the world's largest, with a storage capacity of 2.2 million barrels, built by Hyundai Heavy Industries and operated in 1,200 metres of water off the Angolan coast.
How do currents affect the shape and accuracy of an oceanographic mooring line?

A mooring line follows a half-catenary curve similar to a kite in the wind, with currents (and wind, if the top buoy is above the sea surface) influencing its shape. If currents are strong, above 0.1 m/s, and the mooring line is long, more than 1 km, the instrument's actual position can vary by up to 50 meters from its nominal location.
What design philosophy distinguishes the hybrid floating offshore platform described from a conventional wind platform with added WECs?

Rather than treating wave energy converters as auxiliary devices bolted onto an existing wind platform, the hybrid concept integrates a wind turbine and three flap-type WECs within a unified hexagonal semi-submersible structure designed from the outset so the wind turbine, platform, and WECs are co-developed to share buoyancy, stability, and energy-harvesting functions.

doc_id: wikipedia:Wind power in the United Kingdom

messages.content: Why did offshore wind receive a higher Renewable Obligation Certificate (ROC) rate than onshore wind in the UK?

Under the Energy Act 2008's banded ROC scheme introduced from April 2009, onshore wind received 1 ROC per MWh while offshore wind received 2 ROCs, reflecting offshore wind's higher costs of generation.
What turbines were chosen for the Vineyard Wind 1 offshore wind farm, and how are they anchored?

The developers selected General Electric's Haliade-X turbines, each capable of producing 13 MW, with a three-bladed rotor between 164 and 222 meters in diameter. The 62 turbines are installed in a grid pattern spaced 1 nautical mile apart and anchored using monopile foundations driven into the seabed.
Which country installed the first offshore wind farm, and when?

Denmark installed the world's first offshore wind farm, Vindeby, in 1991. By 2010 there were 39 offshore wind farms across the waters of Belgium, Denmark, Finland, Germany, Ireland, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, and the United Kingdom, with a combined operating capacity of 2,396 MW.
What was the turbine specification and voltage of the inter-array cables used in the Hornsea wind farm construction?

The construction specification used 165 turbines, each rated at 8 MW, giving a rated capacity of 1.4 GW. The inter-array cables, supplied by JDR Cable Systems and installed by Seaway 7, operate at 66 kV.
What is the capacity and turbine configuration of the Sunrise Wind offshore farm?

Sunrise Wind is a 924 MW utility-scale offshore wind farm that will consist of 84 Siemens Gamesa 8.0-167 turbines, each with a 167 meter rotor diameter and 8.0 MW capacity, located on the Outer Continental Shelf to supply power to New York.
What makes the Green Volt offshore wind farm notable, and what challenge does it face?

Green Volt, located about 80 km off Scotland's East Coast, was the world's largest floating offshore wind farm when consented in April 2024, at 560 MW from 35 turbines each rated at 16 MW, and is described as Europe's first commercial-scale floating offshore wind farm. However, as of August 2025 its future is problematic as cabling costs to shore have increased.
How does the two-level auto-optimization control framework for wave energy converters work?

The high-level controller operates at a longer time scale to maximize average energy generation over several wave periods, and generates a Power Take-Off (PTO) profile as a reference for the low-level physical system to follow, leveraging parameterization of the non-stationary ocean operating conditions.
Why is fault detection particularly challenging for floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs)?

FOWTs operate in a hostile marine environment with restricted accessibility and maintainability, and currently there is no all-encompassing fault detection architecture deployed on them, which poses a major challenge for reliability engineers and can lead to increased operations and maintenance costs.
What does the simplified nonlinear dynamical model for a semi-submersible floating wind turbine (FWT) need to capture?

The model needs to capture the complex interplay between rotor dynamics and the finite rotations of the floating platform, in order to address the critical challenge of performance degradation under combined wind and wave loads before FWTs are constructed.
Why does a wave energy converter shape optimization study compare shapes of the same area rather than the same volume or weight directly?

Shapes of the same area are compared because the overall cost of ships and offshore structures is roughly proportional to their weight, so for a wave energy device to have a comparable price to another design, keeping the area equal is used as the basis for finding the optimum shape that produces maximum power under a specific incident wave condition.
Why does offshore wind turbine maintenance accessibility involve stochastic rather than purely scheduled planning?

Environmental conditions evolve both seasonally and randomly, so the value of a given environmental state for maintenance depends not just on whether a maintenance task can be performed now, but also on where the system sits within the seasonal accessibility cycle and how likely favorable conditions are to follow, since the same turbine condition can have different accessibility status at different times.
What is needed for floating offshore wind to achieve cost parity with fixed-bottom offshore wind?

Techno-economic cost modeling suggests floating offshore wind can achieve comparable or lower costs than fixed-bottom offshore wind, but this requires simultaneous development of multiple innovations in floating system design, focused on volume production, standardization, industrialization of the supply chain, and leveraging global industry experience.
Why are some marine control systems over-actuated, and what problem does this create?

Some marine control systems are over-actuated to guarantee reliability and high performance. Because there are more actuators than strictly needed, allocating the desired force and moment demand to actual actuator commands becomes an optimization problem, known as control allocation.
What does wave filtering remove in a course autopilot system?

Wave filtering removes the first-order oscillatory wave-induced motion from the autopilot's heading angle, heading rate, and rudder angle signals, so the control system does not react to the oscillatory wave motion itself.
How many thrusters does a typical AUV use, and how many degrees of freedom of force can they generate?

A typical AUV can have 1 to 5 thrusters, which, combined with the action of servos, generate forces across five degrees of freedom (the roll degree is not considered), with all forces and torques measured relative to the AUV's center of mass.

doc_id: local:Switched control system design an experimental test on underwater robotic vehicle.doc

messages.content: Why is a cascaded switched control system used for an ROV performing pipeline inspection?

A single fixed controller cannot fully satisfy the desired closed-loop response, because performance suffers significantly when the ROV must perform both station-keeping and pipeline tracking at points that emphasize nonlinearities and hydrodynamic uncertainties. A cascaded switched control scheme, using multiple controllers, is needed to remain robust to these hydrodynamic uncertainties.

doc_id: local:A Cascaded Nonlinear Heading Control with Thrust Allocation An Application on an Underactuated Remotely Operated Vehicle.pdf

messages.content: How does the cascaded nonlinear heading control scheme for an underactuated ROV combine thrust allocation and heading control?

It uses an inner loop based on thruster allocation, which relies on the vehicle's velocity feedback to detect the change in thrust required for maneuvering, and an outer loop based on nonlinear PD heading control, applied to generalized ROV models for decoupled horizontal and vertical plane motions.
What control method is proposed to suppress stick-slip vibration in a drill string?
A sliding mode controller combined with torque feedforward is proposed to control stick-slip vibration in a drill string.
What is the two-loop control architecture used for the unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) in this study?

The control architecture uses an outer loop of auxiliary kinematic control based on the UUV's position and orientation state errors, and an inner loop of sliding mode control based on the velocity state vector. The cascade system integrates backstepping technology with sliding mode control and a fuzzy logic component, and addresses environmental disturbance by introducing a filtered random error input.
What two sliding mode control approaches are compared for polytopic uncertain systems in this paper?

The paper addresses sliding mode control design using both a traditional variable structure control (VSC) with a relay-type function and a unit vector control (UVC), proposing suitable state transformations so the closed-loop dynamics can be rewritten to derive LMI-based design conditions, with the VSC case based on a Persidskii diagonal-type Lyapunov function candidate.

doc_id: local:CASCADED SWITCHING SUPERVISORY CONTROL OF NONLINEAR UNDERWATER ROBOTIC VEHICLE FOR  PIPELINE TRACKING.pdf

messages.content: What causes the perturbation terms in the nonlinear ROV model used for pipeline tracking?

The perturbation terms in the system's state and input functions arise from the hydrodynamic added mass and damping forces, with upper bounds for these perturbations determined separately for the mass and damping matrix components.

doc_id: local:Estimation of the Hydrodynamics Coefficients of an ROV using Free Decay Pendulum Motion.pdf

messages.content: What experimental method was used to estimate the hydrodynamics coefficients of the ROV II, and why was it modified from the classical approach?

A free decay test was used, but with the usual spring oscillation replaced by a pendulum motion, because it is difficult to determine the hydrodynamic forces of an underwater vehicle directly, especially the added mass and drag coefficients. The experimental results from the free decay test of a scaled model compared well with simulation.
What mathematical tool is used to derive stability conditions for the sliding mode control of Markovian jump systems with time-varying delay?

A stochastic Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional candidate is combined with Jensen's inequality and a free-connection weighting matrix method to derive sufficient delay-dependent conditions for stochastic stability, expressed as linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), and a sliding mode control law is then synthesized to ensure the closed-loop system's state trajectories reach the specified sliding surface in finite time.
How is the center of pressure (COP) of each fin represented in the torpedo AUV control surface model?

Three coordinates precisely locate the center of pressure of each fin relative to the vehicle's center of mass, giving a flexible representation that lets users match the number of fins and their locations to real-world torpedo AUV designs, with a positive deflection angle defined as a positive rotation of the control surface about an axis.
How does the Virginia Tech 690 AUV estimate its location, and what sensor does it use?

The 690 AUV estimates its location using DVL-aided inertial navigation. It is equipped with a Doppler velocity log (a TELEDYNE MARINE Pathfinder) with four acoustic beams at a 30 degree Janus angle, which records the distance from the DVL sensor to the lake bed along each beam at a rate of 10 Hz.
What power control challenge did the Blueye X3 ROV platform face, and how was it addressed?

The Blueye X3 could only be turned on and off by an external magnet placed near a reed switch behind its LED array. To address this, an electromagnet was installed at the end of the docking funnel, controllable via the processor bottle, enabling remote activation or shutdown instead of relying on continuous power to avoid the robot drifting away while unreachable.
What is an atmospheric diving suit, and what structural features does it typically have?

An atmospheric diving suit is a small submersible with a pressure hull that accommodates a single occupant at an internal pressure of about one atmosphere, addressing the major physiological stresses the underwater environment imposes at depth. It typically has hollow arm spaces with pressure-resistant joints for manually operated manipulators, and separate articulated leg spaces for locomotion, resembling a bulky suit of armor or an exoskeleton.
What did the USV Maxlimer accomplish during the Ocean Discovery X Prize competition?

Maxlimer deployed a HUGIN autonomous underwater vehicle to map 278 square kilometres of seafloor in the Mediterranean Sea off Kalamata, Greece, in 24 hours during the late-2018 competition, an accomplishment that made the GEBCO-NF Alumni Team the winning team.
What is the tradeoff an AUV faces when choosing its altitude during a seabed pipeline search?

A higher altitude gives the AUV a wider field of view, increasing its chances of finding the pipeline, and a lower probability of thruster failure since seaweed is less likely to wrap around thrusters. However, the altitude from which the AUV can perceive the seabed depends on water visibility, so in low visibility it cannot perceive the seabed from a high or medium altitude, meaning it is not always possible to operate at the preferred altitude.
How have non-profit organizations used ROVs for underwater debris removal and detection?

Clear Blue Sea proposed the FRED (Floating Robot for Eliminating Debris) vehicles, though the FRED platform is not an underwater vehicle. Separately, the Rozalia Project has used underwater ROVs equipped with multibeam and side-scan sonars to locate trash in ocean environments.
Why is an AUV's sensing region modeled as either a sphere or a cone during mission planning?

Each AUV's sensing region is modeled as a sphere or cone because factors limiting sensor range, such as occlusions, salinity, and water temperature, are mostly unknown at the planning stage, so these simple shapes are set conservatively in size to account for the unknown factors, though more complex shapes could also be relevant.
What does the autonomy of unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) depend on, and why does it remain an unsolved problem?

USV autonomy profoundly depends on perception capability, particularly in busy maritime traffic, near the coast, or in inland waters. Despite important advances in maritime computer vision for USVs, reliable perception in these conditions remains an unsolved problem.
What AUV platform was used for the sea trials near Haifa, and what are its operational capabilities?

The trials used Snapir, a modified ECA Group A18D midsize autonomous underwater vehicle configured for deep-water research. Snapir is capable of autonomous mission execution at depths up to 3000 meters with an operational endurance of 21 hours.
What sensor fusion coupling strategies are identified for underwater vehicle localization, and what challenges remain unsolved?

Fusion techniques are categorized into loose, tight, and ultra-tight coupling strategies, requiring efficient data association and preprocessing such as image enhancement and color correction to maintain localization accuracy. Unsolved challenges include the lack of semantic understanding in mapping, the absence of adaptive decision-making during exploration, and limited real-time computation capability on resource-constrained underwater vehicles.
What is nRTIS, and how does it achieve high-resolution 3D acoustic imaging while staying compact?

nRTIS (nano-scale Real-Time Imaging Sonar) is a compact 3D ultrasonic sensing system with a total aperture diameter of just 30, integrating a circular array of 16 MEMS microphones around a central ultrasonic transducer controlled by an RP2350 dual-core microcontroller. It achieves high-resolution 3D acoustic imaging in a small form factor by handling real-time data acquisition on the embedded hardware while offloading the advanced spatial filtering and beamforming computations to an external host system.
Why is reconstructing seafloor surface shape from 2D sidescan sonar image intensities a mathematically ill-posed problem?

With sidescan sonar, the exact range to the seafloor is known from the two-way travel time of the signal, but the beam angle is not known because the transducer array is arranged along a single line. Traditionally, shape-from-shading techniques have been used to derive the seafloor surface from the way reflected signal intensities change with incidence angle, but this reconstruction from 2D intensities alone remains mathematically ill-posed.
Why was the Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm chosen over 3D feature descriptors for template matching with sonar data?

Traditional 3D feature descriptors such as PFH were used for template matching, but the sonar data in this use case was highly noisy, which made feature descriptors unreliable for robust feature computation. A direct alignment strategy using ICP was adopted instead, alternating between establishing point correspondences and estimating the rigid transformation between point clouds.
What sensor and environmental parameters determine side-scan sonar (SSS) resolution?

SSS resolution depends on the horizontal beamwidth, sonar range, and the speed of sound. Along-track resolution, in the direction of vehicle travel, and across-track resolution, along the range axis, are calculated separately, with across-track resolution based on the bandwidth of the sonar CHIRP signal used.
Why did vision-based SLAM methods fail during the ROV field test at the USMMA marina, and what method was used instead?

The marina environment exhibited high turbidity, and vision-based approaches including LSD-SLAM, ORB-SLAM3, and COLMAP were unable to find sufficient features in the optical imagery to produce a reconstruction. As a result, the proposed approach was compared only against a stereo sonar reconstruction method.
What do the Northern Adriatic Reefs and Seafloor Sediments side-scan sonar datasets each offer, and what is a limitation?

The Northern Adriatic Reefs dataset offers georeferenced side-scan sonar mosaics of biogenic reefs off Venice, capturing broader geological formations, though its whole-mosaic format may not be well suited for training models to detect specific objects. The Seafloor Sediments dataset includes over 434,164 images from side-scan sonar waterfalls along the coast of Catalunya, valuable for its scale and seafloor-type diversity.
What is the field of view and resolution of the imaging sonar used in the experiments?

The sonar has 512 horizontal beams spanning a 130 degree horizontal field of view and a 20 degree vertical field of view, recorded at 10 FPS and stored as a 512x398 image, where each pixel holds an 8-bit intensity value for its corresponding horizontal beam and range bin. During the experiments it was configured with a 2 meter maximum range and a gain setting of 10.
What is the tradeoff between multibeam sonar and forward-looking/imaging sonar for underwater 3D sensing?

Multibeam sonars can provide dense 3D point clouds but are often expensive and bulky. Forward-looking and imaging sonars are more affordable and compact, but this comes at the cost of only producing planar slices of the environment, limiting their ability to capture 3D structures without sufficient vehicle motion.
What testing procedure was used to verify the reliability of electrical and sensor connections before full system integration?

All subcon and epoxy connections underwent a 24-hour submersion water test, and electrical components such as the cameras and sonar went through these same tests. Components were tested individually before full system integration tests were performed to ensure the software could use all of the electrical data, and extended-duration runs of the integrated system helped catch wiring and power distribution issues.
What is a key risk of perceptual aliasing in a distributed, graph-based pose SLAM system with inter-robot loop closures?

If scene descriptors from different robots appear similar, point clouds are exchanged between them, so perceptual aliasing, mistaking different locations as the same, can overwork the communications link even though steps are taken to prevent it from corrupting the SLAM solution.
What sensor suite does the customized BlueROV2-heavy robot use for navigation and perception?

The vehicle uses a Rowe SeaPilot Doppler velocity log (DVL), a VectorNav VN100 inertial measurement unit (IMU), a KVH DSP-1760 3-axis fiber optic gyroscope, a Bar30 pressure sensor, and a pair of wide-aperture multi-beam imaging sonars, a Blueprint Subsea Oculus M750d and M1200d, with the M750d used as the horizontal sonar, for perception.
What detection range and coverage has diver detection sonar (DDS) demonstrated against intruders?

DDS has demonstrated 360 degree coverage with detection ranges of 300 to 800 meters against intruders wearing open-circuit breathing equipment, which is significant given the area of open water and the many possible entry points into harbors. Non-random false alarms can be caused by non-threat underwater contacts such as large fish, schools of fish, or marine mammals.
What experimental setup was used to validate CFD codes for violent free surface flow on a ship-like deck structure?

A simplified ship-like structure in model scale was used, with comprehensive experimental studies covering three geometries and multiple regular waves impacting the structure. Pressure was measured at ten locations on the deck in front of a breakwater, specifically for validation of various CFD codes against violent free surface flow.
What numerical schemes and algorithm does the OpenFOAM CFD study use for spatial discretization, time discretization, and pressure-velocity coupling?

The study uses second-order centred schemes for spatial discretization and a second-order backward scheme for time discretization, with the numerical system resolved using a Pressure-Implicit with Splitting of Operators (PISO) algorithm, implemented using the finite-volume, open-source OpenFOAM software.
What does the OpenFOAM CI pipeline's automated single-timestep test check for?

The CI pipeline checks OpenFOAM log files for warnings and errors, automatically detecting and running any tutorial cases added to the repository for a single timestep. Since running all simulations for only one timestep takes very little time, this test can be run frequently and helps ensure there are no setup errors in the test cases, while also uncovering some errors in the code that can only be detected when OpenFOAM actually runs.
How does the two-way actuator-line coupling model the hydrodynamic force between a flexible beam and the surrounding fluid flow?

A quasi-steady Morison-type drag closure evaluates the hydrodynamic line force using the fluid velocity sampled at a prescribed offset upstream of each beam control volume, and the equal and opposite reaction is projected back into the fluid momentum equation through a normalised Gaussian kernel, with the beam discretised by a cell-centred finite volume method sharing the same mesh and time loop as the flow solver.
What is the basis for the Reynolds stress term in the new subgrid-scale stress model for large eddy simulation?

The Reynolds stress is obtained analytically from a Cinlar random velocity field, based on vortex structures observed in the ocean at the subgrid scale, and is validated against turbulent channel flow computed in OpenFOAM, compared with the commonly used Smagorinsky and one-equation eddy subgrid-scale models.
What three CFD solver methods are compared in terms of million lattice updates per second (MLUPS)?

The comparison covers an in-house solver using the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM), Nek5000 using the spectral element method (SEM), and OpenFOAM using the finite volume method (FVM), measuring absolute and normalized MLUPS as a function of grid number on both uniform and non-uniform meshes.
How do perfect-slip and no-slip bottom boundary conditions differ in their treatment of velocity near the water-air interface in the OpenFOAM simulation?

Perfect-slip boundary conditions retain a nonzero tangential wall velocity, whereas no-slip conditions connect to zero velocity through a thin wall-affected region. The resolutions tested agree closely through the resolved interior, with the largest differences appearing near the water-air interface.
How does ChatCFD's physical-fidelity evaluator judge whether an OpenFOAM run is correct?

The physical-fidelity evaluator scores an OpenFOAM run against physically meaningful conditions on the converged field, including mass and momentum conservation, integral force balances on wall patches, and agreement with reference profiles for canonical validation cases, so a case that runs to completion but converges to a physically incorrect steady state is correctly assigned a lower score than one that converges to the intended flow.
Why does reduced precision CFD computation show different speedups for different problem sizes?

The computational gain from reduced precision varies significantly depending on the CFD application's characteristics and computational load per core, in particular how much the application is bounded by memory or MPI-related communications. A lid-driven cavity test in single precision showed near-expected speedup only for larger computational loads of 166k cells per core, while smaller test cases of 40k cells per core showed much smaller gains of 1.1 to 3x.
What is the geographic jurisdiction of the Port Alberni Port Authority?

Under the Canada Marine Act, the Port Alberni Port Authority, created in 1999, is responsible for the Alberni Inlet from the Somass River to Tzartus Island, and the port regularly receives large oceangoing cargo vessels, tugs, fishing boats, and search and rescue vessels.
What time-duration variables are tracked to characterize a vessel's total stay in port?

The stay-time characteristics include T1 (wait time for the mooring spot), T2 (wait time for start of operation), T3 (operation time), T4 (wait time for unberthing), with T2+T3+T4 giving mooring time and T1+T2+T3+T4 giving the vessel's total time in port, alongside the arrival, mooring, unblocking, and operation start/end dates and hours.
What is a major criticism of the National Invasive Species Act (NISA)?

A major criticism is that NISA does not reach far enough because, by focusing so heavily on ballast water, it neglects other significant pathways of invasive species introduction, even though it broadened its predecessor NANPCA's scope and introduced new strategies promoting collaboration, research, and education.
What was the first successful refrigerated cargo ship, and what did it transport?

In 1876, French engineer Charles Tellier fitted the cargo ship Eboe with a methyl-ether refrigerating plant of his own design and renamed it Le Frigorifique, which successfully imported a cargo of refrigerated meat from Argentina.

messages.content: When was the SAR Convention adopted and when did it enter into force?

The International Convention on Maritime Search and Rescue (SAR Convention), a maritime safety convention of the International Maritime Organization, was adopted on 27 April 1979 and entered into force on 22 June 1985, with later amendments made by IMO resolutions in 1998 and 2004.
What did the Erika III maritime safety package address, and what incident motivated it?

Erika III, the third and final maritime safety package, addressed civil liability and flag states. It was motivated partly by the Prestige oil spill, which showed existing regulations were inadequate; EU officials argued the spill could have been avoided had the earlier Erika I and II proposals been fully implemented.
How did China's state-run maritime shipping company, founded in 1961, develop into COSCO?

China established a state-run maritime shipping company in 1961 and signed shipping agreements with many countries to lay the foundation for the country's ocean transport. That organization developed into the present-day China Ocean Shipping (Group) Company (COSCO), supported by heavy government investment in water transport infrastructure and increased mechanization and containerization at major ports.
Why do surface defects like corrosion pits and fatigue cracks act as effective stress raisers in stress corrosion cracking?

Stress at a surface is highest at the root of a notch or imperfection, so cracks grow most rapidly there. Corrosion pits and fatigue cracks act as effective stress raisers, and at surface defects that are sufficiently deep, the electrochemical potential differs from that at the surface, with the composition and pH of the solution within the defect also altered by electrochemical effects.
Why did landlocked Switzerland establish its own maritime fleet?

Switzerland first recognized its need for merchant ships during World War I, and a further supply crisis during World War II forced it to deploy ships worldwide, leading it to establish its own fleet flying the Swiss flag in 1941. The venture proved successful, so the fleet, home-ported in Basel, was retained after the war.
How was Foremost Group's first jointly-financed cargo ship construction funded in 2015?

In 2015, Foremost began construction of its first cargo ship jointly financed by banks in both the People's Republic of China and Taiwan, with the Beijing office of China's Export-Import Bank and the New York branch of Taiwan's First Commercial Bank each providing equal loan facilities to support construction of two 180,000-dwt bulk carriers.

doc_id: wikipedia:Ballast water regulation in the United States

messages.content: What approach did the 2011 National Research Council study recommend for setting ballast water discharge standards?

Since determining the exact number of organisms that could launch a new invasive population is complex, the study suggested an initial step of establishing a benchmark for organism concentrations in ballast water below current levels, then using models to analyze experimental and field-based data to inform future discharge standard decisions.
Why does a more realistic sensor model for container ship control exclude direct surge and sway velocity measurements?

The more challenging sensor configuration omits surge and sway velocities because, in practice, GPS is available on container ships but directly measuring absolute velocities is more difficult, making noisy measurements of other states a more realistic representation of onboard sensing.
What operational scenario is analyzed in the study of a floating dock's de-ballasting with a malfunctioning pump?

The study performs a dynamic analysis of the de-ballasting operations of a floating dock when one of its pumps malfunctions, examining how the dock's dynamic behavior is affected during this abnormal de-ballasting scenario.
What is the recommended frequency and purpose of capsize training for intermediate sailors?

Intermediate sailors are encouraged to capsize their dinghies at least once in a safe, supervised location to become acquainted with their boat's floating properties and the capsize process, so that in the event of an uncontrolled capsize, they can recover the boat and its occupants using established procedures.
What are the primary methods for righting a small monohull and a catamaran after capsizing?

Most small monohull sailboats can be righted by standing or pulling down on the centreboard, Daggerboard, or bilgeboard to lift the mast clear of the water, with the boat's righting moment usually engaging once the mast is around 30 degrees from horizontal. For catamarans, the crew stands on the lower hull and pulls back on a righting line fed over the upper hull; in small catamarans like the Hobie 16, at least one crew member must assume this task quickly to prevent the boat from turtles and becoming difficult to recover.
What is the impact of increasing the coefficient beyond 6 in the reward function?
Increasing the coefficient beyond 6 may cause numerical instability due to larger gradient steps, resulting in deviations from the target direction during navigation.
What happens when the coefficient exceeds 3?

When the coefficient exceeds 3, we observe a significant asymmetry in the stroke patterns, rendering the navigation strategy ineffective because the swimmer prioritizes energy conservation over advancing toward the target, leading to a decrease in navigation accuracy.
What is the primary focus of the section titled 'Estimation of Natural Vibration Frequencies of Ship's Hull'?

The primary focus of the section titled 'Estimation of Natural Vibration Frequencies of Ship's Hull' is the calculation and analysis of natural vibrations in ship hulls, which is a critical aspect of ship and marine engineering design, as referenced in the document from 2013.
How many times is the section 'Estimation of Natural Vibration Frequencies of Ship's Hull' referenced in the passage?
The section 'Estimation of Natural Vibration Frequencies of Ship's Hull' is referenced three times in the passage, as indicated by the repeated use of the same heading at positions 25, 27, and 27.
What is the main focus of the section titled 'Cost Estimating: Voyage Costs –Specific Voyage Costs'?

The main focus of the section titled 'Cost Estimating: Voyage Costs –Specific Voyage Costs' is on the detailed estimation of specific voyage-related costs in ship operations, which are integral to the broader economic analysis of ship design and operational efficiency.
Which document section provides a continuation of the discussion on fuel oil (FO) consumption in voyage cost estimation?

The document section titled 'Cost Estimating: Voyage Costs –FO Consumption (cont.)' provides a continuation of the discussion on fuel oil (FO) consumption in voyage cost estimation, building upon the initial analysis introduced in 'Cost Estimating: Voyage Costs –Specific Voyage Costs'.
What is the primary purpose of using turbulence models in AUV design?

The primary purpose of using turbulence models in AUV design is to account for the effects of turbulent flow, which is essential for accurately predicting hydrodynamic performance and forces acting on the vehicle.
Which turbulence models were mentioned in the passage and what are their specific applications?

The passage mentions several turbulence models including low-Re version of two-equation models used to capture low turbulence levels in the viscous sublayer and damped turbulence; a nonlinear two-equation model for cross flow interaction at higher angles of attack; the SST (shear stress transport) model used to study the effect of free surface on drag and lift coefficients at different submergence depths.
How many ships were originally planned in the Bayern class, and which four ships comprised it?
The Bayern class was originally planned to consist of four dreadnought battleships, and they were Bayern, Baden, Sachsen, and Württemberg.
Which two ships of the Bayern class were completed, and why were the others not?
Only Bayern and Baden were completed. The other two ships, Sachsen and Württemberg, were not completed due to shifting war priorities that favored U-boat production over battleship construction.
What happens to the flow characteristics downstream of the sail as it progresses toward Sensor F4 and F5?

The flow characteristics downstream of the sail gradually return to a canonical equilibrium state as it progresses toward Sensor F4 and F5. The excess energy observed near the sail, which is confined to low frequencies corresponding to the convection of horseshoe vortex legs and sail wake eddies, diminishes significantly by the time the flow reaches Sensors F4 and F5. The RMS levels and spectral shapes at these downstream sensors virtually collapse with the bare hull data, indicating that the boundary layer has recovered and the influence of the sail is negligible.
Why are Sensors F4 and F5 considered as Zero Pressure Gradient references?

Sensors F4 and F5 are considered as Zero Pressure Gradient references because the RMS levels and spectral shapes of the flow at these locations are virtually identical to those of the bare hull data. This indicates that the boundary layer has returned to a stable, canonical equilibrium state, with no significant influence from the sail's presence. The recovery of the flow characteristics confirms that these downstream locations are free from the disturbances caused by the sail, making them suitable as reference points for zero pressure gradient conditions.
What were the primary design goals for the Flight IIA destroyers?

The primary design goals for the Flight IIA destroyers were to be more economical than Flight III, reflecting the expectation of lower-intensity warfare, while retaining Flight III's helicopter facilities. This was achieved by removing non-essential systems such as Harpoon missile launchers and AN/SQR-19 TACTAS, with the possibility of reinstallation if needed. The focus was shifted toward land attack, littoral warfare, and reduced operating costs, with most designs featuring a reduced cell count and some using a smaller hull.
What systems were removed from Flight IIA compared to Flight III, and why?

The Harpoon missile launchers and AN/SQR-19 TACTAS were removed from Flight IIA compared to Flight III due to the anticipated lower-intensity warfare environment. These systems were deemed unnecessary for the expected operational conditions. The Phalanx CIWS was also removed, as it was planned to be replaced by the RIM-162 ESSM system. These modifications were part of efforts to reduce costs and streamline the vessel for the new operational role.
What is the title of the book authored by Alain Demerliac that focuses on the nomenclature of Louis XIII and Anne d'Autrich era warships?
Nomenclature des Vaisseaux de Louis XIII et de la régence d'Anne d'Autriche, 1610 a 1661.
What is the English title of the book translated by François Fougerat, originally authored by Jean-Claude Lemineur?
The Sun King's Vessels
What is the primary purpose of the Independence class of littoral combat ships?

The primary purpose of the Independence class of littoral combat ships is to serve as smaller, agile, multipurpose warships designed to operate nearshore in the littoral zone for the United States Navy.
How many ships were initially approved for the Independence class, and how many were ordered by March 2016?
Initially two ships were approved for the Independence class, and by March 2016, the Navy announced an intention to order an additional two ships, increasing the order to 13 ships total.
What is the WEST system and what are its key characteristics?

The WEST system is a hardwood construction method used in yacht building, involving plies of wood strips that are soaked in epoxy and applied over the boat frame. It results in a durable, lightweight, and robust hull.
What are the advantages of fiberglass construction for mass-produced yachts?

Fiberglass construction is ideal for mass-producing yachts due to its use of molds. The hull is made from plies of roving and matting soaked in resin, with decks often featuring a balsa or PVC foam core between glass mat layers. However, both the hull and deck are susceptible to water intrusion and blister formation below the waterline.
What is the velocity probability distribution for the case when α = -1/2?
The velocity probability distribution for the case when α = -1/2 is given by P_0(q) = 2^-1/4 e^-πq^2 / √(2).
What is the integral expression for the case when α = 0?
The integral for the case when α = 0 is given as L(t) ∝t^1/3 and P_0(q) = 2^-2/3 3^-1/3 Γ( 2/3, 2 q^3/3 ).
How is the morphing fin mechanism actuated?

The morphing fins are actuated by a servo-driven push rod mechanism housed within a free-flood chamber, with two servos controlling the retraction/deployment and articulation of the fins, allowing for a 20 degree angle of attack.
Where are the electrical cables routed to control the morphing fins?
The electrical cables are routed through two watertight channels located on either side of the free-flood chamber that houses the morphing mechanism.
What is the main limitation of optimization methods based on CFD that rely on surrogate models?

The main limitation of optimization methods based on CFD that rely on surrogate models is that they often construct models based solely on shape parameters rather than the full hull geometry, which results in an incomplete representation of the input/output relationship and restricts their applicability to entirely different ship types.
What is the current need regarding the collaboration between simulation experts and ship designers?

The current need is to increase the overlap between simulation experts and ship designers by implementing a Computer-Aided Design (CAD) engine-based 3D surrogate model, which would allow designers to rapidly evaluate design choices, reduce project throughput time, and decrease the workload on simulation specialists.
What is the goal of computing the convex hull for a finite set of points?
The goal of computing the convex hull for a finite set of points is to construct an unambiguous, efficient representation of the required convex shape.
What are some output representations that have been considered for convex hulls of point sets?

Output representations that have been considered for convex hulls of point sets include a list of linear inequalities describing the facets of the hull, an undirected graph of facets and their adjacencies, or the full face lattice of the hull. In two dimensions, it may suffice more simply to list the points that are vertices, in their cyclic order around the hull.
What materials are commonly used in the construction of a RIB hull, and what is the purpose of each?

The hull is made of steel, wood, aluminium, or a combination of wood for the structure and glass-reinforced plastic (GRP) composite for the shaped and smooth surface. Some manufacturers also weave Kevlar into the GRP sheets for extra strength. The GRP provides a smooth surface that enhances hydroplaning, while the structural components like wood or steel provide durability.
What are the differences between deep-V and shallow-V hulls, and how do they affect the boat's performance?

Deep-V hulls cut through waves easily but require greater engine power to start planing. Shallow-V hulls plane at lower speeds but offer an uncomfortable ride. Modern RIB hulls often combine a deep V at the bow with a broad planing pad, which flattens out to provide a stable surface for planing, balancing performance and comfort.
What is the main focus of the article titled 'An insight about roll damping within the second generation intact stability criteria'?

The article focuses on the role of roll damping in the context of second generation intact stability criteria for ships, discussing how semi-empirical methodologies have been developed to estimate the damping influence on ship roll motion, and noting that while CFD methods are theoretically suitable for predicting roll damping, they are not widely used.
What are the two primary authors mentioned in the article?
The two primary authors mentioned in the article are Nicola Petacco and Andrea Pollicardo.
What is the name of Hull's local daily newspaper?
The Hull Daily Mail.
How is the fluidic contribution to the mirror self-gravitational potential determined?

The fluidic contribution to the mirror self-gravitational potential is determined by the free-surface shape, which is derived from capillary balance that includes the same potential. This creates a nonlinear problem solved iteratively, starting from a self-gravitation-free equilibrium shape, evaluating the potential, updating the interface via an equilibrium solver, and repeating until convergence is achieved.
What method is used to evaluate the complete elliptic integrals in Eq.?

The complete elliptic integrals in Eq. are evaluated using Carlson's symmetric forms, with parameters clamped to 0.0 to avoid singularities, and this clamping has no measurable effect on the converged shape.
Where was the first Iliria-class patrol vessel, Iliria (P 131), built?
The first Iliria-class patrol vessel, Iliria (P 131), was built in Gorinchem, Netherlands by Damen Group.
What is the name of the cannon equipped on the Albanian Iliria-class patrol vessels?
The Albanian Iliria-class patrol vessels are equipped with a remote-controlled 20mm Nexter M621 NARWHAL Cannon.
What is the class of the patrol vessel described in the passage?
The Chiayi-class patrol vessel is a heavy patrol vessel of the Coast Guard Administration of Taiwan.
What facilities are included in the medical center of the Chiayi-class patrol vessel?
The medical center has a negative pressure area, a surgery suite, and an X-ray facility.
What initial condition is considered to study the transition between behavior 1 and behavior 2?
A small initial horizontal displacement of the bubble from the pit axes and therefore from its rest conditions.
At what pressure do the pit-clusters forces become repulsive and the noise increase?
Above pressures of 150 kPa.
What was the original purpose of the LVTPX12 prototype, and how did it evolve?

The LVTPX12 was a personnel carrier prototype originally equipped with a 20 mm M139 autocannon and 7.62 mm M73E1 machine gun. It evolved into the LVTP7, which became the standard personnel carrier model.
What distinguishes the LVTR7 from other variants in the LVT7 series?

The LVTR7 is the recovery variant within the LVT7 series, characterized by being unarmed and equipped with a winch and crane for recovery operations. It does not carry armament, unlike other variants such as the LVTP7 and LVTC7, which are armed with machine guns or autocannons.
What are the main cleaning technologies discussed in the review article on underwater ship hull cleaning?

The main cleaning technologies discussed in the review article include rotary brushes, high-pressure and cavitation water jet technology, ultrasonic technology, and laser cleaning technology. These methods are applied to both dry-dock and underwater cleaning processes.
What is the primary focus of the article by Changhui Song and Weicheng Cui?

The primary focus of the article is to provide a comprehensive review and analysis of ship hull cleaning technologies, detailing their applications, mechanisms, and relevance in marine engineering contexts.
What does the symbol 'a' represent in the context of ship volume calculations?
The symbol 'a' represents the volume of passenger spaces.
What is the significance of permeability in ship stability calculations?

Permeability is significant in calculating the floodable length, which determines the length of ship that needs to be flooded starting at a given point along the ship in order to cause the ship to sink to the waterline, using Shirokauer's method. Standardized values of permeability are used to calculate the total volume of the flooded compartment, and thus the floodable length, from the change in water displacement caused by flooding that compartment.
What is the expression for the total energy in the given passage?
The total energy is computed through the integral of the quantum Hamiltonian operator, where the asterisk denotes the complex conjugate.
How is the evolution of the particle's mean-squared displacement described in the passage?

The evolution of the particle's mean-squared displacement is described by the second moment of the probability density function, which is derived with respect to the radial coordinate in the coordinate system located at the center of the domain.
What is the required size and color scheme for the circular disc marking on the ship's side?

The circular disc must be twelve inches in diameter and painted on each side amidships or as near thereto as is practicable, with a horizontal line eighteen inches in length drawn through its centre. The disc must be in white or yellow on a dark ground, or in black on a light ground.
What does the center of the circular disc indicate?
The center of the disc indicates the maximum load-line in salt water to which the owner intends to load the ship for that voyage.
What was the primary purpose of the Guided Missile Cruiser Baseline (CGBL) design?

The primary purpose of the Guided Missile Cruiser Baseline (CGBL) design was to create a cruiser with the combat capabilities of VLS-capable Ticonderoga-class cruisers (CG-52 onwards) while incorporating DDG-51 (Arleigh Burke-class destroyer) hull standards and technology.
How did the CGBL design differ from the Ticonderoga-class cruiser in terms of size and design philosophy?

The CGBL design was considerably larger than the Ticonderoga-class cruiser due to increased margins and reserves for weight and mission growth throughout the anticipated service life, reflecting a more robust and flexible design philosophy compared to the Ticonderoga-class.
What is the focus of the study regarding the modular packed bed reactor?

The study focuses on gas flow through an experiment-scale modular packed bed reactor composed of square bars arranged in layers, with each layer rotated by $30^\circ$, leading to complex void space geometries. Particle Image Velocimetry measurements at particle-based Reynolds numbers of 100 and 200 are used to validate particle-resolved numerical simulations employing boundary conforming meshing and the blocked-off method for solid boundaries.
How do the flow characteristics inside and above the bed behave at Reynolds numbers of 100 and 200?

The flow inside the bed is largely independent of the Reynolds number and is determined by the geometry of the void spaces. In the freeboard, the flow is dominated by slowly dissipating jets downstream of the bed, which exhibit unsteady oscillations at the higher Reynolds number of 200. Numerical simulations using both the Eulerian-Lagrangian and Eulerian-Eulerian approaches show good agreement with measurements inside the bed but stronger deviations in the freeboard, attributed to numerical properties of the simulation methods.
What does full load departure represent in terms of vessel loading?

Full load departure represents a condition where the vessel is loaded with all systems charged, including fresh water, cooling, lubricating, hydraulic, and fuel service header tanks, piping, and equipment filled with their normal operating fluids. Crew and effects are at normal values, consumables such as provisions, potable water, and fuel are at 100% capacity, and ammunition and/or cargo is at maximum capacity. The vessel is operating at its limiting draft or legal load line.
How is the full load departure condition used in marine engineering?

The full load departure condition is used as a reference state in marine engineering to define the maximum loading state of a vessel, ensuring it is operating at its legal load line with all systems fully functional and maximally loaded with necessary fluids and cargo. It serves as a critical benchmark for calculating stability and performance under extreme operational conditions.
What is the title of the book by John D. Alden that provides a photographic history of the U.S. Navy's steel-hulled ships?
The title of the book by John D. Alden is 'American Steel Navy: A Photographic History of the U.S. Navy from the Introduction of the Steel Hull in 1883 to the Cruise of the Great White Fleet .'
What is the ISBN number of the book 'American Battleships 1886–1923: Predreadnought Design and Construction'?
The ISBN number of the book ' American Battleships 1886–1923: Predreadnought Design and Construction ' is 978-0-87021-524-7.
What factors should users consider when selecting a model structure for CLS maneuvering?

Users should consider the importance of motion estimation accuracy, the modular structure of MMG models, the hydrodynamic basis of each module, the need to adjust interaction and modification coefficients for force balancing, and the availability of captive model test and particle image velocimetry data for validation.
Why is there no de-facto standard model for CLS maneuvering?

Because many different models have been proposed, and the choice depends on the user's specific requirements, making it necessary to compare and validate each model using empirical data such as captive model tests and flow field measurements.
What is the design requirement for ships with the highest Finnish–Swedish ice class, 1A Super?

Ships with the highest Finnish–Swedish ice class, 1A Super, are required to maintain a minimum speed of 5 knots in a broken brash ice channel with a thickness of 1.0 metre (3.3 ft) in the middle and a consolidated (refrozen) ice layer of 0.1 metres (3.9 in).
How do ships of lower ice classes 1A, 1B, and 1C differ in their operational assumption compared to the highest ice class?

Ships of lower ice classes 1A, 1B, and 1C are assumed to rely on icebreaker assistance for operation in difficult ice conditions, whereas ships of the highest ice class, 1A Super, are designed to operate in difficult ice conditions mainly without icebreaker assistance, though they are still assumed to require icebreaker support from time to time.
Why were the two sections of the ship not found close to each other at the bottom?

The two sections of the ship were not found close to each other because the vessel did not break apart upon striking the bottom; instead, the stern rolled over on the surface, spilling cargo and landing on portions of the cargo itself, which resulted in the separation of the sections. The angle, repose, and mounding of clay and mud at the site indicate this mechanism rather than a direct collision at the bottom.
What evidence supports the stress fracture hypothesis?

The stress fracture hypothesis is supported by the testimony of former crewmen, including Richard Orgel, who described the ship's behavior during storms as resembling a diving board, and by George H. 'Red' Burgner, who testified that a loose keel contributed to the vessel's loss and that hull failure occurred due to undue stress, as indicated by the cracking and splintering of the white enamel paint on the side tunnels.
What is the primary concern of a naval architect regarding a vessel's operation?

The primary concern of a naval architect regarding a vessel's operation is hydrostatic stability, which is essential for ensuring the safety and performance of the ship in both water and air environments.
How do marine engineers address the issue of shifting weight in vessels?

Marine engineers address the issue of shifting weight by balancing fuel and ballast water, using water stored in ballast tanks to counteract imbalances caused by the movement of liquid inside the vessel.
What is the primary function of active fin stabilizers on cruise ships and yachts?

The primary function of active fin stabilizers on cruise ships and yachts is to reduce the vessel's roll, either while underway or, in the case of zero-speed systems, while at rest, by extending beyond the hull below the waterline and altering their angle of attack based on heel angle and rate-of-roll, similar to airplane ailerons.
How do zero-speed stabilizers differ from typical active fin stabilizers?

Zero-speed stabilizers differ from typical active fin stabilizers by functioning while the vessel is not underway, whereas typical active fin stabilizers operate only when the vessel is moving. Zero-speed systems achieve this by using specially designed fins that move with sufficient acceleration and impulse timing to counteract roll, enabling stabilization at rest.
What is one method by which ultrasonic transducers can help reduce marine fouling on small to medium-sized boats?
Ultrasonic transducers can initiate bursts of ultrasonic waves through the hull medium to kill or denature algae and other microorganisms that form the beginning of the fouling sequence.
On what types of boat hull materials can ultrasonic systems not be effectively applied?
Ultrasonic systems cannot work on wooden-hulled boats or boats with a soft-cored composite material, such as wood or foam.
What is a fast attack craft (FAC) primarily designed for?
A fast attack craft (FAC) is primarily designed for offensive operations, typically operating in close proximity to land, and is armed with anti-ship missiles, guns, or torpedoes to engage敌方 vessels.
What are the typical characteristics of a fast attack craft (FAC) in terms of size, speed, and operational limitations?

A fast attack craft (FAC) has a displacement under 700 tons, can reach speeds of 25+ knots or 46+ kph, and due to its size and design, lacks the seakeeping capability and all-round defensive systems necessary for extended operations in open ocean environments; it is usually restricted to coastal or nearshore missions.
What generates a righting moment in a normally loaded vessel during rolling?
A righting moment is generated by the increased volume of water displaced by the hull on the lowered side of the vessel when it rolls from perpendicular.
What causes the free surface effect in a ship with partially full bulk cargo compartments?
The free surface effect occurs when liquid inside partially full compartments moves in response to the vessel's motion, shifting the center of gravity and reducing stability.
What is the primary goal of the autonomous vessel design described in the passage?

The primary goal of the autonomous vessel design is to collect marine debris to mitigate the negative effects of marine pollution, particularly the accumulation of plastics and industrial waste, thereby protecting human health and biodiversity.
What tools and technologies are used in the design and simulation of the autonomous vessel?
The design and simulation of the autonomous vessel are based on MATLAB Simulink and supported by an Arduino-based control system.
What is the primary purpose of the International Code of Signals?
The International Code of Signals is mandatory for carriage on ships and is used for communications between all ships, including merchant vessels and naval vessels.
Which conventions are specifically mentioned as being related to maritime safety, pollution prevention, and operational standards?
